claims.text: Grafana stores no metrics of its own: each panel sends its query to a data source (here Prometheus) and draws the returned series; Prometheus does the scraping and storage.
claims.source_hint: Grafana docs: Data sources; Panels and visualizations; examples/don-hang @ stage-2 datasources.yml comment

claims.text: Grafana reads provisioning files (data sources, dashboard providers) from /etc/grafana/provisioning when it starts; docker-compose.yml@stage-2 mounts ./deploy/monitoring/grafana/provisioning there and ./deploy/monitoring/grafana/dashboards at /var/lib/grafana/dashboards, both read-only.
claims.source_hint: Grafana docs: Provision Grafana (data sources, dashboards); examples/don-hang @ stage-2: docker-compose.yml:259-275

claims.text: datasources.yml@stage-2:1-12: apiVersion 1; data source Prometheus, uid prometheus, type prometheus, access proxy, url http://prometheus:9090, isDefault true; the file also lists a second (Loki) data source.
access: proxy means the Grafana server sends the queries to the data source URL (not the browser).
claims.source_hint: Grafana docs: Provision data sources / data source access mode (proxy = server)

claims.text: dashboards.yml@stage-2: provider donhang, folder Đơn Hàng, type file, allowUiUpdates false, options.path /var/lib/grafana/dashboards; with allowUiUpdates false, changes made in the UI cannot be saved over the provisioned dashboard.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: deploy/monitoring/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/dashboards.yml; Grafana docs: Provision dashboards (allowUiUpdates)

claims.text: donhang-api.json@stage-2 has four timeseries panels: 'Requests per second, by status code' (sum by (code) (rate(http_requests_received_total[5m]))), '5xx responses per second', 'p95 response time' (histogram_quantile(0.95, ...)), 'Orders placed per second'.

A panel's queries are under targets (a panel may have several; each Đơn Hàng panel has one); datasource.uid selects the data source, expr is the PromQL query, legendFormat {{code}} names each series after its code label.
claims.source_hint: Grafana docs: Prometheus data source, query editor (Legend {{label}}); dashboard JSON model (targets)

claims.text: Because the dashboard is a JSON file in the repository and provisioned (Grafana also rescans the provisioned folder while running), a machine that pulls a change gets it at the latest on the next Grafana start; a UI-only dashboard lives in that Grafana's own storage.
claims.source_hint: Grafana docs: Provision dashboards; Dashboard JSON model

claims.text: When you start monitoring an API, request rate, error rate and response time are a common first set of panels because together they give a rough picture of what its users experience; fewer panels answering clear questions are read faster.
claims.source_hint: Grafana docs: Dashboard best practices (RED method); Prometheus docs: Instrumentation (online-serving systems)

claims.text: Grafana service @stage-2: port 3000 published, admin password GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD from GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env; sign in as admin; folder Đơn Hàng contains dashboard 'Đơn Hàng API' (verified via Grafana API 2026-09-30).

Try it: each metrics-endpoint.sh run requests product 999 (404); the dashboard refreshes itself every 10s (refresh "10s"), so within about half a minute the first panel shows or raises a 404 line (scrape 5 s, rate over 5m).
If the prometheus container is stopped, Grafana still opens the (file-provisioned) dashboard, but every panel's query returns an error instead of data, so no panel draws any line.
claims.source_hint: Grafana docs: Data sources (query errors / No data); principle
